skipped.message: Not automatable: Connect a CAN analyzer or oscilloscope to the powertrain CAN bus and measure the bit time of frames sent by the cluster (2 µs per bit for 500 kbit/s). Confirm the cluster communicates without error frames on a 500 kbit/s bus.

Not automatable: Force a bus-off on the cluster with a CAN fault-injection tool, such as a short of CAN-H to CAN-L or error-frame injection. Then confirm with a bus trace that the cluster resumes transmitting ClusterStatus according to the recovery timing in the network management document.

Not automatable: Drive EngineSpeed on the bench at several values (for example 0, 1000, 4000, 8000 rpm) and visually check that the tachometer needle points to the matching value on the 0 to 8000 rpm scale.

Not automatable: Set RedlineRpm to a known value in the cluster configuration, then visually check that the red zone of the tachometer scale starts exactly at that rpm mark; repeat with a second configured value.

Not automatable: Step FuelLevel from 0 to 100 % on a HIL bench and visually confirm the gauge is drawn as a bar graph with exactly eight segments that fill up as the level rises; compare with FuelBarSegments once a level-to-segment mapping is specified.

Not automatable: Feed FuelLevel with a slow oscillation around a constant mean (simulating incline or slosh) and watch whether the fuel bar or FuelBarSegments stays steady; repeat in a vehicle on a grade.

Not automatable: Apply supply power to the cluster while a high-speed camera films the display and a scope logs the supply line; measure the time from power-up to the first visible frame and check it is within 2 s ("within 2 s of power-up"). Repeat several cold starts.

Not automatable: Film the display with a high-speed camera during speed and RPM sweeps and visual-heavy scenarios; review for stutter and dropped frames, and ask for a measurable frame-rate criterion.

Not automatable: Run worst-case bus load and display scenarios while measuring CPU load with a debugger/trace or OS profiling tool; compute the average over every sliding 1 s window and check it never exceeds 70 percent.

Not automatable: On a bench cluster with a known trip value, select a trip counter. Press OK for clearly less than 2 s and check the counter is not reset. Then press OK for clearly more than 2 s and check on the display that the selected trip counter resets and the other trip counter is unchanged. Use a stopwatch or a timed button actuator.
Not automatable: Check whether the cluster menu offers a display theme option. If it does, select each theme and confirm by eye that the display theme changes.

Not automatable: Bring the cluster into SLEEP (IGN OFF, wait until after the goodbye phase). Measure the battery supply current with a precision ammeter or power analyzer over a settled period. Verify it does not exceed 0.1 mA.

Not automatable: With a diagnostic tester, send a write-memory request (e.g. WriteDataByIdentifier / WriteMemoryByAddress) without security access and confirm a negative response (security access denied). Then unlock via SecurityAccess seed/key, repeat and confirm the write is accepted. Also try a wrong key and confirm the write is still refused.

Not automatable: Clarify the requirement with the security team (e.g. keys stored in an HSM / secure storage, not readable via debug or diagnostics). Then do a security review and penetration test: try to read keys via diagnostic memory reads, the debug interface and a flash dump, and confirm no key material is exposed.

Not automatable: Activate a red telltale (BrakeWarn = 1) and an amber telltale (MIL = 1) at the same time and visually check on the cluster that the red telltale is given priority as defined in the display specification.

Not automatable: Connect a diagnostic tester to the diagnostic connector and flash a new, validly signed software version. Then read the software version identifier with the tester and confirm that it matches the new version.

Not automatable: Use a diagnostic tester to attempt one update with a validly signed image and one with an invalid or tampered signature. Confirm that only the validly signed image is installed, using the software version read-out and the tester's negative response for the invalid image.

Not automatable: Note the installed software version. Start an update with a diagnostic tester and interrupt it, e.g. by disconnecting power or the tester mid-transfer, or by sending a corrupted image. Restart the cluster and confirm that the previous version is reported and that the cluster resumes normal operation, e.g. ClusterStatus transmitted with ClusterState ACTIVE.

Not automatable: Induce a backlight driver fault on the bench (e.g. open the backlight LED string or use fault injection hardware), then read the fault memory with a diagnostic tester and check that the expected DTC is stored.
Not automatable: With at least one known DTC stored, connect a diagnostic tester, issue a read-DTC request and check that the stored DTCs are returned correctly.

Not automatable: Power up the cluster (IGN on) and watch the display (camera or by eye) to confirm the self-test sequence runs. Also confirm through a diagnostic tester or debug interface that the self-test executed.

Not automatable: Feed a constant VehicleSpeed (e.g. from a simulator), switch the unit setting between km/h and mph in the cluster menu, and check visually that the display shows the correct value and unit label for each setting.
Spec rejected by a person

Not automatable: For a received message, stop sending it for 450 ms, then for 550 ms. Confirm the cluster treats its signals as invalid only in the second case, using the reaction defined for that signal (for example the telltale behaviour in 7.4).
